How to try this release
=======================

The release page itself has a "Start here" table: for each thing you can try (the shop program on Windows or Linux, the website, the Android app, the Studio) it names
the file to download and gives the steps. This file is the longer test plan for NextGenOS staff.

Where things are (all on this release page):

  NextGenOS-Setup-Studio-<version>-windows.zip / -linux.zip   the Setup Studio for NextGenOS staff, with its own Node.js. Never for a customer.
  SmartRetailPOS-Hub-Setup-<version>.exe                      the Hub's Windows setup
  SmartRetailPOS-Hub-<version>-win-x64.zip                    the same program as a plain folder; open it with "Start Business Hub" (no black window). The setup is the normal way.
  smart-retail-pos-hub_<version>-1_amd64.deb / _arm64.deb     the Hub's Linux packages
  website-<customer>-windows.zip / -linux.zip                 the online shop, built for one customer, with its own Node.js (Windows: double-click Start Website; Linux: ./start-website.sh --app)
  SmartRetailPOS-<kit>-<version>.apk / .aab                   the Android app (signed with a one-off test key unless ANDROID-SIGNING.txt says otherwise)
  base-kit.json                                               the list the Studio reads: which file is which, and its fingerprint
  SHA256SUMS.txt, BUILD-STATUS.txt                            check your download; which parts were built

If the release says TRIAL, the programs were built WITHOUT licence keys, only to try the installing. They can never be activated: the Hub shows its "needs a licence"
page and nothing more. Never give a trial to a customer.

PART A: the Studio (about 15 minutes)
-------------------------------------
1. Download every file of the release into ONE folder (for example C:\release). Unzip the Studio zip somewhere else.
2. In the folder "NextGenOS Setup Studio", double-click "Setup Studio" (the icon with the blue box; Linux: ./setup-studio.sh). The Studio opens in a window of its own:
   there should be NO black terminal window. Windows may say "Windows protected your PC" (the program is not signed yet): "More info", then "Run anyway".
   Check: open it a second time while it is open (it should only bring up the same window); close the window (the Studio should be gone: the Task Manager shows no node.exe).
3. Make the administrator account (a name and a password of at least 8 characters). In Settings add a salesperson and a reviewer.
4. Sign in as the salesperson. Add a customer (three questions), fill in the details, choose a look and a machine. Watch the picture of the program change.
5. Prepare the setup and send it for approval. Sign in as the reviewer and approve it. (The person who prepared it cannot approve it: try.)
6. As the administrator: Settings, "The programs folder", type the folder from step 1, "Check and save". It should say "Version <version>: N files checked".
7. As the reviewer: the customer's "Installer" step. If the release is a trial, tick "only to try". Press "Make ...'s pack" and download the zip.
8. Open the pack. Read "START HERE.html" and "READ ME FIRST.txt" in the shop-computer folder: do they say the right things, in words an owner understands?

PART B: the Windows setup on a real Windows 10 or 11 PC (about 10 minutes)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. In the pack, open "1 - Shop PC (Windows)". Keep the setup file and the "profile" folder together.
2. Double-click the setup. Say Yes to the permission question. Windows warns about an unknown publisher until the setup is signed: "More info", "Run anyway".
3. On the last page leave "Open Smart Retail POS now" ticked and press Finish. A small window says "Smart Retail POS is starting" (it can take up to a minute), and then Smart Retail POS opens
   in a window of its own, with no address bar, showing a page that says the program needs a licence, with a place to type a key.
   That is the correct result for a trial. It must NOT open in your usual web browser. Tell us if it does, or if it shows anything else, or if it asked you to install something first.
4. Restart the PC. Right after the restart, press the Smart Retail POS icon on the desktop at once, before the PC has settled: the small "starting" window should appear and the program should
   open by itself when it is ready. It must never show "This site can't be reached".
5. For a "touch-screen till" customer the program should also open full screen by itself after the restart.
6. Uninstall it (Settings, Apps). The folder C:\ProgramData\NextGenOS stays on purpose: the shop's information is kept.

PART C: Linux (Ubuntu 22.04/24.04, Mint 21+ or Debian 12+)
-----------------------------------------------------------
1. Make the customer's machine "Linux" in the Studio and make a new pack. Copy "1 - Shop PC (Linux)" to the Linux PC.
2. In a terminal there: sudo ./install.sh   (be online for this step)
3. Open Smart Retail POS from the applications menu: it opens in a window of its own and shows the "needs a licence" page. Reboot: it should still be there.
4. Remove it with the Software app. /var/lib/nextgenos stays on purpose.

WHAT TO TELL US
---------------
 - Anything that asked you to install something first (that is a bug).
 - Any word on any screen you did not understand.
 - Anything that looked wrong, on either system.

NOT BUILT YET
-------------
 - A website for every customer: the release holds the website of ONE customer (the brand kit of the build). Another customer's website is built from that customer's public settings; the Studio's pack says how. The Windows website was only checked by the build machine, not on a real PC.
 - The AI assistant's setup is not part of this release. It reads the Windows POS database, not the new Hub's data.
 - A signed list of release files: the Studio checks files against fingerprints, which catches damaged downloads, not forged ones.
 - Code signing of the setup (needs the owner's certificate).
